Timeline A.lost_opportunity: the chance to work with a cutting-edge startup and be part of its early growth stages
Timeline A.missed_identity: the version of myself as a bold and daring entrepreneur
Timeline A.emotional_cost: the recurring feeling of 'what if' and wondering if I'm missing out on more exciting opportunities

Timeline B.lost_opportunity: the stability and security of a traditional corporate job
Timeline B.missed_identity: the version of myself as a risk-averse and cautious professional
Timeline B.emotional_cost: the stress and anxiety of dealing with the unpredictability of a startup environment

Timeline C.lost_opportunity: the chance to have a more balanced work-life balance and prioritize personal relationships
Timeline C.missed_identity: the version of myself as a more laid-back and easy-going person
Timeline C.emotional_cost: the burnout and exhaustion from constantly pushing myself to meet high expectations

letters.Timeline A: Dear you, I'm writing to you from 10 years in the future. I'm grateful for the memory of our family vacation to Goa in 2025, where we spent 7 days relaxing on the beach and recharging our batteries. One thing that was harder than expected was dealing with the monotony of a 9-to-5 job. My advice to you is to take calculated risks and don't be afraid to try new things, like I wish I had done when I was 25 and had the opportunity to join a startup. Looking back, I realize that I played it too safe, and it's okay to take a chance and see where it takes you.
letters.Timeline B: Dear you, I'm writing to you from 10 years in the future. I'm grateful for the memory of our team's launch party in 2027, where we celebrated our product's success with over 100 guests. One thing that was harder than expected was navigating the ups and downs of the startup world. My advice to you is to be adaptable and resilient, and don't be afraid to ask for help when you need it, like I did during our company's funding crisis in 2028. Looking back, I realize that joining a startup was the best decision I ever made, and it's given me the opportunity to grow and learn in ways I never thought possible.
letters.Timeline C: Dear you, I'm writing to you from 10 years in the future. I'm grateful for the memory of our company's IPO in 2030, where we raised over $1 billion in funding. One thing that was harder than expected was dealing with the pressure to constantly perform and meet high expectations. My advice to you is to prioritize your mental and physical health, and don't be afraid to take a step back and recharge when you need to, like I did during my burnout in 2029. Looking back, I realize that I pushed myself too hard, and it's okay to take a break and focus on your well-being.

comparison.common_patterns: all three timelines involve a trade-off between stability and risk, and the importance of adaptability and resilience in achieving success
comparison.key_differences: the level of risk-taking and the emphasis on personal growth versus financial success
comparison.hinge_point: the decision to join a startup or not, which determines the level of risk and uncertainty in one's career path
